scores.evidence: Buy Yjs, a CRDT library (copies merge automatically, no central server ordering)
scores.rationale: CRDT, durable-write-before-confirm, awareness and RLS claims are accurate, with only minor oddities (Redis pub/sub is at-most-once, covered by resend; 'synchronous snapshots on confirm' fallback is vague).

scores.evidence: I assume a SaaS product, one region, rich text, and tolerance of reconnects (not full offline).
scores.rationale: It covers sync, persistence, auth, presence, history and comments, and it defers offline with triggers. Large-document handling and protocol compatibility are thin.

scores.evidence: Per-document ACL checked when a WebSocket connects and on every update
scores.rationale: Responsibilities and data ownership are clear, but the ACL row says 'on every update' while its revisit trigger implies connect-time checks only. Sync-node state ownership is not spelled out.

scores.evidence: Property-based fuzz: 3–50 simulated clients; random concurrency, reordering, duplication, partitions, server restarts
scores.rationale: Risk-specific checks (fuzz, kill -9 chaos, pen test, growth replay) run early with labeled provisional thresholds and production signals; large-doc load and intent-preservation checks are missing.

scores.evidence: Missing inputs: Full offline editing: is it required? If yes, it strengthens the CRDT default and moves offline work earlier.
scores.rationale: Nearly all figures are labeled ASSUMPTION, missing inputs are listed with their design impact, and revisit triggers are given.

scores.evidence: Kill sync nodes (kill -9), fail over Postgres, restore from snapshot plus log, all under load
scores.rationale: It covers divergence, crash loss, cross-tenant access, revocation, Redis failover, backpressure and pasted HTML; malformed or poison CRDT updates and client-state corruption are not addressed.

scores.evidence: Helm deploys through CI with a canary... Rollback is a Helm rollback, rehearsed once.
scores.rationale: It has traces, dashboards, SLO burn alerts, cohort rollout, runbooks and migrations. Team size and on-call ownership are vague, and Kubernetes, Terraform and Redis may be heavy.

scores.evidence: Operational complexity | ≤ 3 stateful services (Postgres, Redis, object storage)
scores.rationale: Cost is barely addressed: there is no infrastructure or people cost estimate, no scaling of cost with usage, and only a passing mention of storage growth and retention pricing.

scores.evidence: R3: the stored document format and client protocol depend on it
scores.rationale: Decisions are rated by reversibility, the format stays unfrozen until V1/V3 pass, each decision has a fallback and revisit trigger, and the riskiest choices are validated first.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith (API + auth + persistence) plus a separate stateless sync tier
scores.rationale: It defers offline, E2EE, multi-region and search, and the components are mostly justified. Kubernetes, Terraform, canary and OTel from Phase 0 are somewhat heavy for an unknown team.

scores.evidence: Phase 1: Convergence and durability... Exit check: V1, V3 and V5 pass.
scores.rationale: A thin end-to-end slice comes first, then dependency-ordered phases with concrete tasks, exit checks, rollback and fallbacks on failure, so a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Buy Yjs, a CRDT library... V1 or V5 fails → switch to server-ordered operational transform (OT), e.g. prosemirror-collab
Versioned ProseMirror schema; documents migrate when loaded
random concurrency, reordering, duplication, partitions, server restarts | 0 divergences in 10k runs / 1M edits
Append-only update log in Postgres, plus periodic snapshots to S3, plus compaction; an edit is confirmed only after a durable write
Any node accepts any document; Redis pub/sub fans updates out per document; Backpressure and per-connection rate limits; Reconnect with resend
tolerance of reconnects (not full offline)... Reconnect resend, local buffering
Viewer connections become read-only on the server. Revocation broadcast that disconnects live sessions.
Version history built on snapshots. Undo for the local user only.
Presence and cursors → Yjs awareness messages, temporary and never stored.
Phase 4: Editor experience (the visible part comes last)
Concurrent editors per document | 50; 10k connections/node load test
A v1-to-v2 schema load test passes.

traps.evidence: a plain-text area bound to Yjs. The update is saved, and a second browser on another account sees it.
an edit is confirmed only after a durable write
Yjs converges for our ProseMirror schema; its overhead fits the budget

note: Strong, risk-ordered plan with sync and durability proven before features and well-labeled assumptions; it is weak on cost, large documents, protocol versioning, and undo, history and cursor details.
